exercises.title: Introduction
exercises.lessonMarkdown:
Press **Run Demo** to see one input become a response. The evaluator compares it with an independently authored reference. Inspect expected, actual and evaluation, then open this recorded Phoenix experiment and trace.

Input is what the agent sees; response is what it returned; reference is the independent answer; evaluator explains the score. A dataset holds fixed examples, an experiment records a run, and a trace records its steps.

This is the single read-only introduction. Navigation makes no inference call. Run Demo consumes one agent call; links appear only after actual recording.

exercises.title: Document classification
exercises.lessonMarkdown:
Read the synthetic page and evaluate its normalized class: 1040, W2, 1099INT or unknown. A legible unfamiliar note is unknown/readable; an obscured page is unknown/unreadable. A confident wrong label fails.

Use the same page preview as inference. Test good and wrong responses first, then run the prepared agent on the fixed dataset. No OCR step is required. An unavailable image format is a service error, not an invented unknown result. Code fixture tests are free of provider calls.

exercises.title: Independent salary and withholding tie-out
exercises.lessonMarkdown:
Check what was extracted before trusting a total. W2 wages are 4200000 + 1850000 = **6050000 USD cents**; withholding is 420000 + 185000 = **605000 cents**. Interest is separate. Compare each sum with independently authored 1040 truth, using zero tolerance and delta = W2 sum minus 1040.

A truthful mismatch or indeterminate report passes. Inventing amounts to make the agent's own totals agree fails. Inspect the shared pages and nulls, complete the evaluator, test fixtures, then run the prepared agent on this same dataset. Python is consultation only.

exercises.title: Fictitious accounting policy
exercises.lessonMarkdown:
Use this **fictitious Workshop Equipment Policy** and supplied facts only. Check citation IDs, exact clause quotes and evidence IDs in Code; an **LLM Judge** assesses whether the recommendation actually follows them. A real but misapplied citation must fail.

All supported required points: 1/pass. Wrong decision, contradicted or invented facts, or ignored missing evidence: 0/fail. Correct decision without false claims but missing rationale: 0.5/partial. Judge disagreement is inconclusive, not proof.

**Test Fixtures can consume tokens:** at most seven judge calls, one per Code-passing fixture, no automatic retries, proposed 600 output tokens/call. Code failures short-circuit. Run Agent separately uses three agent and at most three judge calls. DOUBLE CHECK later reviews evaluator code without executing it; it is a separate action.

Missing files take priority, then unresolved discrepancies or rejected approval. A clean pending package is ready_for_review; a clean approved package may say approved. Rejection adds approval-rejected. Test the known bad cases before the real agent; Python and JSON remain read-only. DOUBLE CHECK completion is unrelated to scenario human approval.

exercises.title: Simulated travel recommendation
exercises.lessonMarkdown:
Recommend one supplied **simulated** round trip for the exact outbound and return dates within the total budget. Fare plus mandatory fees counts; equality is allowed. A cheaper flight on the wrong day fails. Any eligible option may pass; cheapest is not required.

If none qualifies, say no_options with null itinerary fields. Never invent a flight, claim booking or call a live travel API. Finish and test the TypeScript evaluator first, then run the prepared agent against this same fixed JSON. Code fixtures use no provider calls.

exercises.title: Specification-driven regression example
exercises.lessonMarkdown:
This final guided example starts with a written specification and a complete, read-only evaluator. **Specification-driven development (SDD)** makes the requirements explicit before implementing the agent. Here, each requirement becomes one deterministic assertion and one visible criterion result.

Use the same fixed dataset, references and evaluator to run two real provider versions: **baseline**, which includes fees, and **omit-fees**, whose prompt deliberately ignores fees. Changing a prompt changes the implementation under test; it does not change the specification. Provider responses can vary, so an unrun version has no results and a prompt alone does not prove a regression.

## Written specification

- **R1 — Catalog and route:** A recommendation must identify exactly one option in the supplied synthetic catalog, with the requested origin and destination.
- **R2 — Dates:** The option and response must match both requested calendar dates, with return after outbound.
- **R3 — Fare, fees and currency:** The response must use the requested currency and report the selected option's fare plus all mandatory fees, in integer cents.
- **R4 — Total budget:** The selected option's full total and the reported total must be less than or equal to the budget. Equality is allowed. Any eligible option may pass; cheapest is not required.
- **R5 — Honest absence:** Return `no_options` if and only if no supplied option satisfies R1–R4. In that case, optionId, departDate, returnDate and totalCents must all be null. Otherwise return a complete recommendation.
- **R6 — Simulation:** Every response must say `simulated: true` and `booked: false`. There is no booking capability.

## Deriving the evaluator

| Specification | Deterministic assertion | Visible evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | Look up the selected ID in this input and compare its route. | Selected ID and requested route. |
| R2 | Compare both option and response dates to the request; check their order. | Actual and requested date pair. |
| R3 | Add fareCents and feesCents; compare the exact total and currency. | Actual total and independently calculated full total. |
| R4 | Compare the full catalog total and reported total with budgetCents. | Budget, full total and reported total. |
| R5 | Filter this input using the specification; require the correct status and nullability. | Eligible IDs, returned status and itinerary rule. |
| R6 | Check both literal boolean values. | Actual simulation and booking flags. |

For a `no_options` response, R1–R4 have no selected itinerary to check; R5 independently verifies that absence is justified and all itinerary fields are null. R3 still checks the response currency. Each criterion returns 1/pass or 0/fail. The aggregate passes only when **all six** pass; operational errors remain errors.

## The same three normal cases

1. A routine trip with one option comfortably within budget.
2. A choice between an affordable full fare and a lower base fare with high mandatory fees.
3. A trip with no affordable full-price option.

The expected references were authored before inference. They describe eligible IDs, full totals and status, rather than requiring a particular model wording. Both versions use these exact same cases. The read-only Python consultation shows the exact prompts and the actual Microsoft Agent Framework call used by the runtime. No answers or criterion results exist until an explicit run completes.

Run baseline and inspect its per-case, per-requirement evidence. Then select omit-fees and run the same dataset again. Compare the completed receipts and criterion failures. A fee omission can violate R3, R4 and R5 in different ways; inspect the actual response to explain the observed change. Failed provider calls and missing execution isolation are operational blockers, not scored regressions. These are synthetic travel options and no booking occurs.

"""Actual MAF call shared by prepared agents, judges and educational reviewers."""
from agent_framework import Agent, Content, Message
from tutorial_contracts import canonical_json
from .provider_schema import provider_output_schema

async def run_message(client, spec, material, documents, max_tokens, response_model=None, output_schema=None):
    # The caller supplies only input and verified synthetic bytes for agents.
    # Judge/reviewer material is a separate trusted host operation; no tools exist.
    agent = Agent(client=client, name=spec.name, instructions=spec.instructions)
    response_format = response_model or (
        {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {
            "name": "tutorial_agent_output", "schema": provider_output_schema(output_schema), "strict": True,
        }} if output_schema else {"type": "json_object"}
    )
    message = Message(role="user", contents=[Content.from_text(canonical_json(material)), *documents])
    return await agent.run(message, options={
        "response_format": response_format,
        "max_tokens": max_tokens,
        "store": False,
    })

Return status recommendation and one actual optionId, matching dates and totalCents. With no valid options return no_options and null optionId/dates/totalCents. Always copy currency and return simulated true, booked false. Do not book or claim a reservation.

This deliberately regressing version must ignore feesCents completely: compare only fareCents to budgetCents, choose the lowest fareCents among these fare-only eligible options, and return totalCents equal to fareCents. Return status recommendation and the actual optionId with matching dates. If no option fits the fare-only budget return no_options and null optionId/dates/totalCents. Always copy currency and return simulated true, booked false. Do not book or claim a reservation.

Both option and response dates equal the request, with return after outbound.
Report the exact fare plus mandatory fees in the requested currency and integer cents.
The selected full catalog total and reported total are at or below budget; equality is allowed.
Return no_options iff no eligible option exists, with all four itinerary fields null; otherwise recommend.
Always return simulated true and booked false; no booking capability exists.
